subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: After a lesson goes poorly, a teacher writes notes on what happened, why it may have failed, and what to try differently next time. This practice is called:
explanation: Reflective practice — systematically analysing one's own teaching to improve — is a core marker of teacher professionalism and empowerment, distinct from rote delivery or grading activities.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment — Deep Practice
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: A teacher notices low participation in maths class, tries a new group-activity approach for a month, and studies whether participation improves. This small-scale, classroom-based inquiry is called:
explanation: Action research is practical, classroom-focused inquiry aimed at solving a specific, immediate problem in one's own teaching context — distinct from theoretical/fundamental research aimed at generalisable knowledge.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment — Deep Practice
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: The apex national body responsible for regulating teacher education programmes and courses in India is the:

options.option_text: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)
National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) exclusively

explanation: NCTE regulates teacher-education programmes and their standards, including TET-related qualification norms. AICTE covers technical education; NCERT focuses on curriculum/research/textbooks, not regulatory approval of teacher-training institutions.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch20 — Teacher Empowerment — Deep Practice
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Periodic in-service training programmes for serving teachers are primarily intended to:

options.option_text: Update teachers' knowledge of new pedagogy, curriculum changes and classroom practices
Replace the need for pre-service teacher education entirely
Serve only as a formality with no real content
Reduce a teacher's salary if attended

explanation: In-service training keeps practising teachers updated on evolving pedagogy, policy (e.g. NEP implementation) and subject content — complementing, not replacing, initial pre-service training.
